note: Loop structures are pieced together from public candidate reports and change often. Treat each as a rough map, not a guarantee, and confirm the current format with your recruiter.

companies.name: Google
companies.program: APM and PM intern

rounds.name: Recruiter call
rounds.detail: A 20–30 minute chat: your background, why PM, why this company, logistics.

rounds.name: 1–2 phone screens
rounds.detail: one product design, one analytical or estimation

rounds.name: On-site
rounds.detail: 4–5 interviews: product design, product strategy, analytical, and a behavioural round ("Googleyness").

companies.format: Case-heavy and conversational. Interviewers push on your reasoning, not your conclusion. Estimation is done out loud with stated assumptions.
companies.whatToKnow: They score structure and trade-off thinking above domain knowledge. Always clarify the goal before designing. Name a North Star metric on every design answer.

companies.name: Microsoft
companies.program: PM intern and new-grad PM

rounds.name: Recruiter call
rounds.detail: A 20–30 minute chat: your background, why PM, why this company, logistics.

rounds.name: 1 phone screen
rounds.detail: product design or a light technical question

rounds.name: Super day
rounds.detail: 3–4 interviews: product design, estimation, behavioural, sometimes a system-reasoning question.

companies.format: More conversational than Google. Interviewers care that you collaborate with them during the case rather than presenting a finished answer.
companies.whatToKnow: Show customer empathy early and check in with the interviewer as you go. Have a favourite Microsoft product you actually use and specific critiques of it.

companies.name: Amazon
companies.region: Global, with a large India intake
companies.program: APM and PM intern

rounds.name: Online assessment
rounds.detail: work simulation and sometimes a writing sample

rounds.name: 1 phone screen
rounds.detail: One 45-minute call, usually a product design or estimation question.

rounds.name: Loop
rounds.detail: 4–5 interviews, each anchored to two or three Leadership Principles, plus product and analytical questions. One interviewer is a bar raiser.

companies.format: Behavioural questions dominate and every story is scored against the Leadership Principles. Expect "tell me about a time" in almost every round.
companies.whatToKnow: Prepare 8–10 STAR stories mapped to the 16 Leadership Principles, each with real metrics. Use "I", not "we". Know Customer Obsession and Ownership cold.

companies.name: Meta
companies.program: Rotational Product Manager (RPM) and PM intern

rounds.name: Recruiter call
rounds.detail: A 20–30 minute chat: your background, why PM, why this company, logistics.

rounds.name: 1–2 screens
rounds.detail: product sense and execution

rounds.name: On-site
rounds.detail: a product sense round, an execution / analytical round, and a leadership and drive round

companies.format: Fast and metrics-first. The execution round is heavy on defining metrics, reading a drop, and trade-offs. Product sense expects a crisp user segment and goal.
companies.whatToKnow: Lead with the user and the goal, then one feature, then metrics. In execution rounds, structure the metric tree before proposing anything.

companies.name: Flipkart
companies.program: APM

rounds.name: Aptitude test
rounds.detail: Timed online test — quant, logic, sometimes verbal. A screening filter.

rounds.name: Group discussion or a case exercise
rounds.detail: A short group case or written exercise to shortlist for interviews.

rounds.name: Interviews
rounds.detail: 2–3 rounds: guesstimates, a product design or improvement case, and a behavioural round.

companies.format: Guesstimate-heavy, India-context. Expect market sizing for Indian cities and tiers, and product cases grounded in Indian e-commerce and logistics.
companies.whatToKnow: Practice estimation with Indian numbers — population tiers, smartphone and UPI penetration, income bands. Know Flipkart's business: marketplace, ads, Flipkart Plus, logistics.

companies.name: Zomato
companies.program: APM

rounds.name: Application
rounds.detail: often with a short written prompt

rounds.name: Take-home assignment
rounds.detail: a product teardown or an improvement proposal

rounds.name: Interviews
rounds.detail: 2–3 rounds: product thinking, analytics, and a founder or senior-leader round.

companies.format: Assignment-led. The written submission is the main filter, so it has to be tight and opinionated. Interviews dig into your assignment and your product instincts.
companies.whatToKnow: Use Zomato and its neighbours (Swiggy, Blinkit, district) heavily and have sharp critiques. The assignment rewards a strong point of view over a balanced survey.

companies.name: Swiggy
companies.program: APM

rounds.name: Assessment or a short assignment
rounds.detail: A screening step before interviews — test or take-home.

rounds.name: Product round
rounds.detail: execution and design

rounds.name: Analytics round
rounds.detail: metrics and a diagnosis question

rounds.name: Hiring manager
rounds.detail: sometimes with a bar-raiser

companies.format: Execution and metrics first. Expect a "a metric dropped, what do you do" question and trade-off discussions grounded in food delivery and quick commerce.
companies.whatToKnow: Be fluent in delivery-marketplace metrics: order frequency, delivery time, contribution margin, rider utilisation, cancellations. Diagnose before prescribing.

companies.name: Razorpay
companies.program: APM

rounds.name: Product case
rounds.detail: often a take-home

rounds.name: Interviews
rounds.detail: 2–3 rounds: product design, analytical, and a culture-fit round.

rounds.name: Technical questions
rounds.detail: Woven through the rounds, given the fintech domain — payments flow, failure handling, compliance.

companies.format: Fintech context throughout — payments, settlements, compliance, B2B. More technical depth expected than at a consumer company.
companies.whatToKnow: Understand how a payment actually flows — gateway, network, bank, settlement — and why failure handling and compliance are product problems, not afterthoughts.

companies.name: Zepto
companies.program: APM

rounds.name: Assignment
rounds.detail: a product or growth problem

rounds.name: Product and analytics interview
rounds.detail: One combined round: a design case plus a metrics question.

rounds.name: Founder or senior-leader round
rounds.detail: A conversation with a founder or senior leader — vision fit, drive, judgement.

companies.format: Fast loop, high bar on ownership. Questions centre on quick commerce under tight constraints: 10-minute delivery, dark-store economics, city expansion.
companies.whatToKnow: Think in unit economics and constraints. Be ready to reason about dark-store density, basket size, delivery cost per order, and what breaks at 10x volume.

companies.name: Meesho
companies.program: APM

rounds.name: Assessment
rounds.detail: Timed online assessment before any interview.

rounds.name: Product case round
rounds.detail: A product design or improvement case, worked live with the interviewer.

rounds.name: Analytics round
rounds.detail: Metrics: define a North Star, read a funnel, diagnose a drop.

rounds.name: Hiring manager
rounds.detail: The manager you would work for. Depth on your assignment and your instincts.

companies.format: Value-commerce context — tier-2 and tier-3 users, low-trust first-time online buyers, sellers who are small businesses. Cases are grounded in that user.
companies.whatToKnow: Design for a user who may be new to online shopping, price-sensitive, and on a cheap phone. Trust, returns, and cash-on-delivery economics come up often.
